title.narrative: Food and Nutrition Social Welfare Program and Project (Capacity Development Project)

description.narrative: ADB has secured a $12 million grant to build on the existing social welfare system and assist the Government in (i) designing and implementing emergency measures that specially target mitigating the impact of the food crisis on the poor and (ii) mid-term measures to address social welfare issues. This will include designing social safety nets that provide assistance directly to the poor, building capacity among stakeholders, and providing technical assistance to reform social welfare strategies in the mid-term.

description.narrative: More efficient and transparent delivery of social welfare and insurance services (including support to food consumption), through strengthened policy, systems, and IT

Average processing time for financial reporting of SIGO reduced by 30% Progress/Status: The average processing time for financial reporting is expected to be reduced through the Core System of SIGO designed to reduce manual processing, enhance the categorization of the primary registration and automate the periodic reporting, and which is expected to be developed by Q4 2020. The business process analysis of social insurance has been conducted by the project consultants in 2016 and 2018, respectively. Data Source: Periodic report (IT system) Actual value:

Satisfaction of population with social protection system increases Achievement: 4 Progress/Status: Two surveys for evaluating the satisfaction of the population with Social Protection were conducted in 2016 and 2018, respectively. The average rate of satisfaction of the population with social protection system was 3.15 points (satisfactory) out of 5 which is very good (G. Tsend-Ayush, the National consultant, 2016). The survey covered 774 respondents from 4 aimags and 3 districts of Ulaanbaatar and focused on 5 aspects such as (I) service delivery and access; (ii) policy and program efficiency; (iii) institutional structural efficiency; (iv) communications skill of the sectorial staff; and (v) client satisfaction with service quality. The next client satisfaction survey was conducted by Maxima consulting firm from September 2017 to March 2018. The survey covered 1,300 households in 9 aimags and 700 households in Ulaanbaatar city on 2 main aspects: (i) satisfaction with the sector policies and programs for 2016-2017; and (ii) satisfaction with social protection and employment services. The 77.2%-94.9% of respondents have evaluated the sector policies and programs as positive; and satisfaction with 72 social protection and employment services was rated as 3.84 out of 5. The services include 32 social welfare /3.55/, 13 health insurance /3.99/, 10 social insurance /3.72/, 7 for population groups /3.99/, and 10 employments services /4.01/. The next survey is planned to be conducted by the Project monitoring and evaluation consultant recruited in July 2020. Data Source: Report on pre- and post- satisfaction surveys directed at beneficiaries and staff

Processing time for hospital claim and application for disability benefit reduced by 20% on average Achievement: 6 Progress/Status: In 2017 the project conducted business process analyses on health insurance and provided recommendations to introduce e-card and web-based service to reduce the processing time for health insurance claim. However, in 2016 the health insurance has been segregated from the social insurance, the project has ceased its activities focused on the health insurance. The application processing time for disability benefit will be reduced once the Core System of SIGO becomes operational. The system will enable web-based access to the social Insurance database and provide immediate service to the clients. In addition, the time for collecting information of applicants such as getting archival references will be reduced once the social insurance archives become digitized and web-based from Q4 2020. Data Source: Periodic report (IT system)

Social welfare reformed and social protection strengthened Indicator: About 10% of the households covered in social welfare programs being implemented based on PMT database are reassessed yearly for eligibility from 2015 Progress/Status: The project supported the GOLWS in conducting the 3rd Household Livelihood Determination Survey based on PMT methodology, which covered over 80 percent or 572.2 thousand households. The report of the PMT survey of 2017 was published by GOLWS in Q1 2020 and available at http://hudulmur-halamj.gov.mn/uploads/files/niigmiin_hamgaalal_20200402.pdf. Re-assessment module of PMT information system was developed under the project in 2018. The PMT consultant delivered the final report with a concept note and materials for the cross-checking the data with other government databases. The system registers and re-assesses households based on their applications. Currently, the PMT database is used for the following 5 social welfare services: 1) Food stamp program; 2) Child money program; 3) Cash allowance for emergency case, allowance for released homeless prisoners, allowance for homeless single parents with 4 or more children under 18 years old; 4) Healthcare services for poor people who needed social welfare supports; and 5) Legal advocacy services for insolvent accused. Data Source: MLSP policy documents Actual value:

Output: 3.2. IT processes and systems are upgraded to deliver more efficient and transparent social welfare and social insurance services Indicator: Consultants and IT support are provided to an Integrated Information System for Social Welfare to be developed by government Progress/Status: The TOR for the new IT system for GOLWS was developed in Q1 2020 by a consultant engaged by the Project. In accordance with the joint resolution by the Minister of Finance and Minister of Labor and Social Protection, the system is to be developed by Customs, Tax and Finance Information Technology Center, a state-owned entity. The required servers and equipment for the integrated system are to be procured with Project support. The integrated welfare information system links two main databases on social welfare /Welfare Information Administration System (WAIS), Household Information Integrated System (based on the PMT data)/ to civil registration and other databases at other Government agencies, and allows application for and electronic transfer of social welfare assistance, benefits to eligible beneficiaries through e-barimt.mn system, which is used to issue VAT refunds. At the time of evaluation, some features of the integrated welfare system rolled out (ehalamj.mn) for 6 social welfare programs provided to over 680 thousand beneficiaries (non-unique). The project supplied desktop and laptop computers valued at $741,331 to GOLSWS central and local offices. Data Source: IT-related project reports and demonstration in SIGO Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y

Output: 3.2. IT processes and systems are upgraded to deliver more efficient and transparent social welfare and social insurance services Indicator: Data monitoring and analysis for SIGO and GOLWS are centralized under MLSP Progress/Status: The Business Intelligence System (BIS) was established at the MLSP by a team of three IT consultants engaged by the project and procurement of software and equipment valued over $1.2 million. The BIS provides access to authorized users at the MLSP to SIGO and GOLWS data servers and pull required data for monitoring and analysis. Users of the BIS acquired skills to use the system through on-site training provided by the consultants. As required by Mongolian laws, the architecture of the BIS was reviewed by the Information Security Department of the Central Intelligence Agency of Mongolia for breach of security for personal information. Data Source: IT-related project reports and demonstration in SIGO and GOLWS Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y

IT processes and systems are upgraded to deliver more efficient and transparent social welfare and social insurance services Indicator: SIGO reporting is fully automated Progress/Status: SIGO accounting policies were updated in accordance with international accounting standards, and reporting templates were developed by the Financial Consulting Firm engaged by the project in 2018. The development of the SIGO Core IT system will integrate financial reporting and will allow for real-time preparation of financial reporting. Reports on revenues, expenditures of social insurance funds, SIGO operational expenses, and the number of beneficiaries will be prepared in real-time when the development of the SIGO Core IT system is completed. Digitization of SIGO archives started in May 2019 is converting paper-based records of insurance contribution payments from 1995 to 2006. At the time of evaluation, this work is in the completion stage. The digitization of the archive will enable social insurance staff to check employment history and reference wages of applicants for old-age pension regardless of their location, reducing application processing time. Data Source: IT-related project reports and demonstration in SIGO Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y
